method: Blind A/B kit from tools/phase0/make-listening-kit.py: both engines' takes rewritten through one float32 WAV writer with identical samples and equal timestamps, random A/B order per pair, key opened only after answers were recorded

engines.reference: YuE2 Python torch-eager BF16 (windows-short-eager / windows-full-eager take 1)
engines.candidate: yue2.cpp f17d526 Q8_0 + F32 VAE, CUDA sm_89 (windows-short-cpp-q8 / windows-full-cpp-q8 take 1)

summary: All four takes passed overall. The C++ Q8 candidate was preferred for both the short and the full fixture. Some audible distortion was reported in one take from each engine.
analysis: The distorted reference take (short A) has no samples near full scale, so that distortion is in the generated audio, not digital clipping

The distorted candidate take (full B) has three isolated samples above full scale near 141.3 s and 144.0 s; three single samples are unlikely to explain audible distortion on their own, so it is probably also generative. Not localized by the reviewer
limitations: One reviewer, one playback system, one take per engine and fixture; not statistically meaningful
Ratings were collected as one overall severity per clip, not per criterion from the scoring sheet
Durations differ between engines (short 78.96 s vs 66.36 s; full 166.12 s vs 169.84 s), so blinding was imperfect
The candidate was clip B in both pairs by random draw, so position and engine are confounded
The question about clipping, asked together with the preference questions, mentioned that the full candidate take has samples above full scale, which may have hinted at an engine
decisionUse: Supports keeping yue2.cpp Q8 as the leading Windows CUDA candidate on quality. Does not by itself set the quality bar, which still needs more takes, reviewers, and the other targets
